english_verification.review_scope: Read the complete A95 source body and original evidence page; checked the current Tag/history, canal mission and sailor decision, and actual English canal-event text. Read the actual local Wiki Markdown chunks, not search excerpts. Reviewed text-only coverage and presentation; no full mission audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.

rationale.colonization: Overseas colonization is not a mission-tree focus.
rationale.complexity: Nobles, sailors, religion, and imperial interaction intersect.
rationale.dark_story: There is an old warlord legacy, but no evidence of large-scale atrocities in the current version.
rationale.difficulty: Requires balancing several political conditions; not tested in an actual playthrough.
rationale.diplomacy: Subjects, relations, and imperial interaction are central.
rationale.early_pressure: A small country, but not a hopeless one; not tested in an actual playthrough.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Religious narratives are present, but magic and artifice are not the primary gameplay focus.
rationale.narrative_density: The River-Reaver past, dynasty, and diplomatic restoration form a connected story.
rationale.tall_play: Canal and administrative development play a sustained role.
rationale.trade_economy: River transport and the sailor system require financial support.
rationale.warfare: Restoring the region still requires some territorial and military action.

identity.appearance: An Esmar River duchy already present in 1444; the scoring table retains an older name rendering.
identity.formation_scope: A95 is an independent starting country; its unique decisions and missions advance under the same Tag.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: The beautiful shores of the Themarenn Lake have always been a popular destination for wanderers in Esmaria, in the old days of the Kingdom of Esmaria it was even the preferred location for the King's residence, with the various river kings making the travel between Esmarainé and Lake Themarenn several times. Ever since the death of the last King of Esmaria, with Esmarainé fallen to the hands of greedy merchants, the Lake has assumed the role of Hub of Esmaria.

description.text: Esmaria is well known for its many rivers, most of which are tributaries of the Esmar River. The river kings were able to use them to connect the region and establish reliable borders for their vassals. Due to the constant stream of visitors, we have been forced to make the most out of the old waterways, resulting in our exceptional ability in navigating them.

description.text: The beautiful shores of the lake attract many visitors. Most of them just come to enjoy the scenery and the fair maidens on its shores, while some come with more hostile intentions. As tensions in the region rise, it is time we finally take up arms to defend our home!

description.text: Seen by their neighbours as no more than brutes who can swim, the River-Reaver Marines gain their name from the renowned Black Castanorian commander Drosten River-Reaver who first occupied Themarenn and much of the central Esmar river for the Sorcerer-King. When the war turned sour he quickly joined the side of the League of Free Realms in 1006, and used his skill in river-fighting to help liberate the rest of Esmaria and push into Escann via the Alen river. After the war he was ordered to give the lands he occupied with his army back to the Esmarians but he refused, and used his River-Reavers to continue to dominate the riverways of the Esmar against his foes. Despite this, thanks to his companionship with the elf Saelihn he was a major force in the elvenization of the region.

description.text: Besieging a fortress is hard. Besieging a coastal fortress is even harder without a fleet. Besieging a fortress completely surrounded by deep water might as well be impossible. Although we aren't able to build stone keeps on water, by constructing small wooden keeps on water that are able to house a few cannons the would-be conquerors will have many difficulties in bringing down our fortresses.

description.text: The Esmari River Parties are famed in all of Cannor. What reaches even the neighbouring regions, from the rebuilt Escann to the far lands of Bulwar, are the feasts by Lake Themarenn. By improving our infrastructure, we will be able to host more guests, and to separate the illustrious ones from the peasants.
description.text_en: The Esmari River Parties are famed in all of Cannor. What reaches even the neighbouring regions, from the rebuilt Escann to the far lands of Bulwar, are the feasts by Lake Themarenn. By improving our infrastructure, we will be able to host more guests, and to separate the illustrious ones from the peasants.

description.text: The Esmarian Kings routinely retreated from the busy court life in Esmarainé to find peace in their palace by the lake. The Lake Palace was left in a state of disrepair ever since the river kings died out, due to its high maintenance cost. But now, as we possess the funds to rebuild and maintain such a splendid palace, we shall show to the whole of Esmaria our great power and wealth.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want pure conquest or dislike relationship and estate requirements.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Hold the riverways, balance nobles and sailors, and use diplomacy and limited wars to expand political influence.
player_overview.overview: Themarenn is a small Esmari river-valley state in 1444, whose ancestors established themselves through force on the rivers. The current mission tree turns this legacy into inland sailors, canals, and noble military service, then seeks to restore regional order through imperial diplomacy and religious branches. There is warfare, but the real distinction is how river administration, dynasty, and politics among the princes are bound together.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy river-valley politics, diplomacy among princes, and stories of local faith.
signature_features: A unique decision switches between sailor and noble recruitment systems.
Canals, inland navigation, and the River-Reaver legacy run through the missions.
Restore Esmaria through imperial diplomacy, subjects, and religious choices.
player_overview.tagline: From a small duchy of River-Reaver descendants to an Esmari principality rebuilt through canals and diplomacy.

reasons: Religious and noble branches add variation.
warnings: Mission requirements are not limited to conquest.
Religious branches are not all available in every campaign.

values.rationale: River infrastructure and diplomatic integration are positive evidence; noble privileges and the priority given to dynastic restoration limit a higher score. Monarchy and ordinary warfare are not treated as evidence of evil; treatment of residents in religious branches has not been fully reviewed.
red_flags: Military noble privileges may take precedence over ordinary residents.
Outcomes of religious and dynastic branches require conditional assessment.
